name: Egg Drop Corn Soup (玉米羹)

ingredients.name: granulated sugar, plus more to taste
kosher salt, plus more to taste

instructions.primary_message: Working over a rimmed baking sheet, shallow pan, or wide tray, hold one end of an ear of corn in your palm and grate the opposite half on the large holes of a box grater, rotating the cob as you work. Flip the ear around and grate the other half in the same way. Use the back of a paring knife to scrape corn cobs directly onto the baking sheet to collect any milk left in the bases of the kernels. You should have about 1 1/2 cups of the grated corn mixture.

Add grated corn mixture to a medium saucepan and set aside. Place the scraped cobs in a large saucepan or pot and add just enough water to cover by about 1.5 cm. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, then reduce heat to medium-low, maintaining a gentle simmer and cooking until fragrant, about 10 minutes. Using tongs, remove and discard the cobs immediately.

Add 2 cups plus 1 tablespoon corn stock to the saucepan with the grated corn mixture. Reserve any remaining stock for another use. Bring to a simmer over medium heat and cook, stirring occasionally, until corn is tender, about 5 minutes. Stir in sugar and salt and adjust seasoning to taste.
In a small bowl, stir together cornstarch and 2 tablespoons of water until smooth. Whisk into broth and bring to a simmer. Cook until soup is lightly thickened and glossy, 30 seconds to 1 minute.

In a liquid measuring cup, beat the egg thoroughly with a fork. Hold the tines of a fork over the spout of the measuring cup. Swirl the soup with a large spoon, then slowly drizzle egg mixture into soup. Remove from heat and allow soup to sit for 30 seconds to allow the egg to finish setting. Serve immediately.

description: This fresh corn soup tastes intensely of sweet summer corn, thanks to two simple techniques.
notes:
Notes: The number of ears of corn needed will vary depending on their size, freshness, and juiciness. For the most consistent results, use the weight of the grated corn mixture in the steps rather than relying only on the number of ears.

Make-ahead and storage: This soup is best served immediately, while the egg ribbons are tender and the corn flavor is freshest. Leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 3 days.
Reheat gently on the stovetop or in the microwave until hot, stirring occasionally. Avoid boiling the soup, which can make the egg tough and the soup overly thick. If needed, add a splash of water or reserved corn stock to loosen the soup before serving.
author: Qi Ai
